title: deterministic-session-trajectory-slicer-and-kernel-occupancy-estimator
author: Eve Park
description:
Motivation: Our existing workload replayers produce high-variance profiling baselines when sequence lengths and batching patterns vary. That noise makes it hard to attribute tail-latency regressions to kernel scheduling vs model changes. This PR adds a deterministic session trajectory slicer plus an offline kernel occupancy estimator that together produce repeatable steady-state runs and a small summarizing artifact used by the perf dashboard.

What this changes: single logical string describing the change—no sub-JSONs. Implements a new replayer module (trajectory_slicer) that slices long session traces into deterministic, time-aligned sub-trajectories, preserving inter-request gaps and token-length distributions. Adds kernel_occupancy tool that consumes runtime telemetry (per-step CPU/GPU utilization, batch sizes, KV cache hits) and outputs a compact occupancy profile used to normalize throughput/latency comparisons across hardware. Adds a reporter that emits a per-cohort summary suitable for downstream p95/p99 stability charts.

Checklist:
- [x] deterministic slicing algorithm (fixed seed, windowed alignment)
- [x] occupancy estimator prototype and unit tests
- [x] integration with the bench harness runner and flamegraph exporter
- [x] docs: README and runbook section describing interpretation of occupancy profiles
- [x] CI: lint, unit, and bench smoke job

Key commits (high-level):
- a1b3cde: initial trajectory slicer implementation and tests
- b4f9e11: kernel occupancy estimator and statistical summarizer
- f0c2d9a: wiring into bench harness, new CLI flags (--slice-window, --occupancy-src)

release_notes: Adds deterministic session trajectory slicer and kernel occupancy estimator. New artifacts: per-cohort occupancy profiles to normalize perf baselines; CLI flags for slicing and occupancy input. Improves reproducibility of steady-state benchmarks and helps isolate kernel-scheduling regressions.
how_to_run: Local quickstart: python -m bench_harness run --trace-path traces/sessions.json --slice-window 30 --output reports/sliced.json; then python -m bench_harness analyze --occupancy reports/occupancy.json; CI bench-smoke job runs with --slice-window 60 and compares occupancy profiles across commits.
performance_observations: On a 4xA100 test cluster, deterministic slices reduced p99 variance of repeated runs from 17% to 4% for a mixed-length conversational workload. Occupancy normalization changed the reported throughput delta vs baseline by ~6% (higher accuracy for kernel-bound regimes).
notes: This PR is intended for benchmark_lab consumers (SRE, perf engineering) and should not affect hosted infra. The occupancy estimator is marked experimental and gated behind --occupancy-experimental CLI flag.
status_notes: Initial CI: bench-smoke failed (numpy mismatch). Fixed requirements and re-run; final CI: all checks passed. Merged after 2 approvals.
testing_instructions: Unit tests included: pytest -q tests/test_trajectory.py tests/test_koccupancy.py. End-to-end: run bench-smoke job in CI or locally via ci/run_bench_smoke.sh.
notes_for_release: Document occupancy profile interpretation in perf dashboard; optional upgrade to bench agents to collect per-step utilization telemetry.
